source.title: Vacuum-relative stability and charge gaps in compact Hamiltonian lattice QED
source.status: Draft dated 29 October 2026; not yet reviewed by specialists.

states.NOT_STARTED: No Lean declaration states this result.
states.FROZEN_UNPROVED: An author-approved Lean statement of the result is frozen with proof `sorry`. This is not proof progress.
states.PROVED: The frozen Lean statement is proved; the build and the axiom audit pass.
states.AUDITED: PROVED, and a statement audit by a reviewer who did not write it confirmed it against the source.

results.label: lem:operator
results.title: Operator realization
results.claim: `H` is self-adjoint with compact resolvent and trace-class heat semigroup; every nonempty Gauss sector reduces `H`; extensive bounds on `H` and `E_0`.

results.label: lem:transfer
results.title: Positivity and the transfer annulus
results.frozen_note: By author ruling R1(a) the frozen statement covers piecewise-constant histories: free steps with constant coefficients, and separate instantaneous kicks (deviation 7).
results.claim: The centered finite-CAR trace `F` is positive, and exactly `d` transfer eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity, satisfy `|λ| ≤ e^{-b m_*}`; the other `d` are their partners `1/conj(λ)`, of modulus at least `e^{b m_*}`.
results.lean_coverage: the frozen statement itself is proved (see `lean/Core/PaperA/`); separately, the older conditional lemmas check the product algebra of form preservation, the inverse-adjoint identity with an explicit inverse, the scalar endpoint implications of a strict β-form drop, and the eigenvector-level inverse-adjoint correspondence
results.outside_lean: histories with time-dependent (continuous or bounded measurable) coefficients on the free intervals, and simultaneous free and kick terms, which ruling R1(a) leaves outside the frozen statement; their reduction to step histories is not formalized.

results.label: lem:fourier
results.title: Canonical Fourier bound
results.frozen_note: By author ruling R1(a) the frozen statement covers piecewise-constant histories (deviation 7); it states `F_0` real and bounds `|F_q|` by its real part (ruling R3).
results.claim: `|F_q| ≤ binom(2d, d+|q|) e^{-b m_* |q|} F_0` for `|q| ≤ d`.
results.lean_coverage: the frozen statement itself is proved (see `lean/Core/PaperA/`); separately, the older conditional lemmas check the finite coefficient estimate inside the proof, that is, the elementary-symmetric bounds and the Vandermonde bound for the antidiagonal correlation relative to the vacuum weight, for every natural `q`
results.outside_lean: the same time-dependent histories (R1(a)); the identification of the Fock-space twist e^{iφQ} with the one-particle kick, which the frozen statement takes as the definition of F(φ).

results.label: thm:main
results.title: Exact physical-sector comparison
results.claim: `E_ν ≥ E_0 + m |Q_ν|` in every admissible integer source sector; `0 < Z_ν(b) ≤ Z_0(b)`, and the binomial thermal bound (4.2) for `m > 0`; the unrestricted auxiliary ground energy equals `E_0`.
results.lean_coverage: the final integration step behind (4.2), for an abstract positive measure and conditional on a supplied factored representation
results.outside_lean: the compact-rotor heat kernel, the Dyson and Feynman–Kac representation, the twisted trace formula, the exact gauge projection and the change of torus coordinates that produces `F_{Q_ν}`, the ground-energy limit, the case `m = 0`, and the identification of the auxiliary ground energy with `E_0`.

results.label: lem:cut
results.title: Cutting with retained rotors
results.claim: `‖H - H_cut‖ ≤ B n_c` with `B = (4r + 2 + 8/g²)/a`, and the cut auxiliary minimum is the sum of the open-block minima.

results.label: thm:vacuum-limit
results.title: Vacuum thermodynamic limit
results.claim: The vacuum energy density `e_vac` exists, with open and periodic finite-size errors at most `3B/ℓ` and `6B/ℓ`.

results.label: prop:cell
results.title: Fixed-cell relative bounds
results.claim: `0 ≤ E_ν^per - E_0^per - m Z_tot ≤ C_cell K` for a fixed periodic source cell, and an extensive electric budget.

results.label: thm:open-source
results.title: Open zero-flux source limit
results.claim: The open zero-exterior-flux source energy density `e_ν^op` exists; along `p | n`, `e_vac + m ρ ≤ liminf E_ν^per(n)/n³ ≤ limsup E_ν^per(n)/n³ ≤ e_ν^op`.

open_in_source.label: eq:bf
open_in_source.note: Hypothesis (BF), a boundary-flux comparison. Paper A states it and explicitly does not prove it; the periodic-source limit is conditional on it.

supporting.name: QEDCore.preservesForm_mul
supporting.step: Product algebra: `U* C U = C` and `V* C V = C` imply `(UV)* C (UV) = C`, in any monoid with a star-multiplication.

supporting.name: QEDCore.preservesForm_one
supporting.step: The identity preserves every form.

supporting.name: QEDCore.preservesForm_list_prod
supporting.step: An ordered product of form-preserving factors preserves the form. That each free evolution and kick preserves `C_5` is a hypothesis.

supporting.name: QEDCore.adjoint_eq_conjugate_inverse
supporting.step: From `C C = 1`, `U V = 1` and `U* C U = C`, derive `U* = C V C`: the identity `U* = C_5 U⁻¹ C_5`, with the inverse supplied explicitly.

supporting.name: QEDCore.no_unit_factor_of_strict_drop
supporting.step: Scalar endpoint implication: `B(T) < B(0)` and `B(T) = t B(0)` exclude `t = 1`. The strict drop itself is a hypothesis.

supporting.name: QEDCore.stable_endpoint_positive
supporting.step: Scalar endpoint implication: with a strict drop, `t < 1` forces `B(0) > 0`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.unstable_endpoint_negative
supporting.step: Scalar endpoint implication: with a strict drop, `t > 1` forces `B(0) < 0`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.stable_annulus_from_endpoint
supporting.step: Division step: `B(0) > 0`, `B(T) = t B(0)` and an assumed integrated bound `B(T) ≤ r B(0)` give `t ≤ r`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.unstable_annulus_from_endpoint
supporting.step: Division step with `B(0) < 0`: the same hypotheses give `r ≤ t`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.inverse_eigenvector
supporting.step: Eigenvector level: `U x = λ x`, `V U = 1` and `λ ≠ 0` give `V x = λ⁻¹ x`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.involution_mulVec_ne_zero
supporting.step: `C C = 1` and `x ≠ 0` give `C x ≠ 0`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.adjoint_inverse_eigenvector
supporting.step: Eigenvector-level inverse-adjoint correspondence: `U* (C x) = λ⁻¹ (C x)`. No multiplicity statement.

supporting.name: QEDCore.elementary_zero
supporting.step: `e_0 = 1` for the elementary symmetric coefficients, defined as subset sums.

supporting.name: QEDCore.norm_elementary_le
supporting.step: `|e_k| ≤ binom(N, k) r^k` when every `|λ_i| ≤ r`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.correlation_zero
supporting.step: The zeroth antidiagonal coefficient equals the vacuum weight `Σ_j |a_j|²`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.one_le_vacuumWeight
supporting.step: `a_0 = 1` implies that the vacuum weight is at least 1.

supporting.name: QEDCore.norm_correlation_le
supporting.step: Termwise bound and Mathlib's Vandermonde identity: if `|a_k| ≤ binom(N, k) r^k` for every `k`, then `|corr_q| ≤ binom(2N, N+q) r^q` for `0 ≤ r ≤ 1` and every natural `q`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.elementary_correlation_bound
supporting.step: The same bound for the elementary symmetric coefficients of `λ`.

supporting.name: QEDCore.relative_correlation_bound
supporting.step: The finite coefficient estimate behind (3.4): `|corr_q| ≤ binom(2N, N+q) r^q` times the vacuum weight.

supporting.name: QEDCore.positive_measure_comparison
supporting.step: The norm of an integrable complex integral is at most the integral of a pointwise majorant against a positive measure.

supporting.name: QEDCore.phase_preserves_bound
supporting.step: A unit-modulus phase preserves a norm bound (removing `e^{-iθ·ν}`).

supporting.name: QEDCore.scaled_coefficient_comparison
supporting.step: Pointwise: phase times nonnegative prefactor times correlation is bounded by the binomial factor times prefactor times vacuum weight.

supporting.name: QEDCore.canonical_integral_comparison
supporting.step: The integrated comparison behind (4.2), conditional on a supplied measure, nonnegative prefactor, unit phase, eigenvalue bound and integrability.
